highlights.title: Sakana AI’s CEO says its homegrown models are about more than Japan’s national security
highlights.summary: Sakana AI aims to strengthen Japan’s industrial competitiveness with homegrown AI models.
body: Sakana AI, a Japanese AI startup, last month revealed plans to develop its own foundation model. The move has drawn attention for its potential impact on Japan’s defense and cybersecurity sectors as well as concerns about reliance on U.S. and Chinese technologies.

Sakana AI’s co-founder and CEO, David Ha, told TechCrunch that its upcoming foundation model, Sawara, is part of the company’s broader goal of supporting and strengthening Japan’s industrial and manufacturing sectors using AI. In addition, Ha noted rising cybersecurity threats and stressed the need for domestic AI alternatives for sensitive applications, particularly if access to foreign models becomes limited.

“When we started planning for this model, of course, we had physical AI, manufacturing, and industry in mind, and we still do. This is our long-term vision,” Ha said. “But short-term, I think Japan has a real need for security-related capabilities as well.”
Sakana will begin working on Sawara this month, aiming to train and release a smaller-scale model in early 2027, followed by a larger version.

highlights.title: So, Did GTA 6 Live up to the Hype?
highlights.summary: Thirteen years — that’s how long players waited to get their hands on Grand Theft Auto 6. The road to Rockstar’s mega-hit was an unusually long one for a bankable franchise video game, but the wait was arguably an even better marketing tactic than that flashy Netflix reveal.
body: While that helped GTA 6 ’s launch reach the loudest crescendo possible, it came with a risk. Too much excitement can be a bad thing. Rockstar Games would have to combat outsized expectations from fans who had convinced themselves that the open-world game would feature a bevy of revolutionary features, regardless of how implausible they were.
Now that the dust has settled and players are cruising around Leonida, I find myself trying to unpack an impossible question: Did GTA 6 live up to all that hype, after all?

On some level, it’s a ridiculous thing to ask. Hype is not a quantifiable metric, so how would you even begin to measure how well it paid off? I suppose we could start by looking at sales data. We already know GTA 6 is a hit in that regard, as Rockstar confirmed that it sold 32.5 million copies in its pre-release period alone. That’s a fairly convincing $3.79 billion answer, right? But there was never any doubt that GTA 6 would be a financial success. If anything, the pre-release sales are actually a reflection of the hype, not the game itself. It’s going to take a few more rounds of post-launch sales figures to gauge success by numbers.

highlights.title: Pensions and benefits services still down after 'cyber incident'
highlights.summary: The UK's former chief technology officer says the Department for Work and Pensions may have been hit by hackers, but the government has not confirmed that.
body: Online benefits and pensions services were still down on Saturday morning following a "cyber incident" which forced the government to take them offline.
The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has not specified what triggered it to shut down access late on Thursday but has not ruled out that it was hit by hackers.

The government has assured benefits recipients and pensioners that usual payments will continue to be made after some claimants reported delays. It is understood the department believes delays were not linked to the cyber incident.
The UK's former chief technology officer David Knott told BBC Newsnight his "strong suspicion" was that the department had been targeted by hackers.

highlights.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
highlights.summary: Aside from dealing with my calendar, there's one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I'm about to miss the bus. What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house.
body: You can have a good time brewing up widgets — as long as you don’t expect too much.

Google announced the ability to create custom widgets using AI back at I/O in the spring. It’s called Create My Widget, and it’s part of Android’s suite of “Gemini Intelligence” features. It’s in beta, and only just started rolling out to Pixel phones earlier this month. I was hyped. Not only does this feature raise tantalizing questions like “What is an app?” and “Where does the app live?” — stuff we live for here at The Verge dot com — it has potential to help me make my home screen ridiculous.

I fired it up on a Pixel 11 Pro and cooked up my first few widgets, including one that shows a different quote from Jurassic Park every hour — the original film, not any of the sequels, naturally. It took about 20 seconds to make, and it rules. Tapping the widget opens a thread in r/MovieQuotes, so there’s not much software magic going on under the hood, evidently. But did it bring me real joy to read the words “That is one big pile of shit,” on my home screen? It did.

highlights.title: Xbox players Angry They Aren't Getting The Next Official Yooka-Laylee Release
highlights.summary: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is skipping Microsoft's gaming platforms, and Xbox players aren't happy because Playtonic has typically released games in this Banjo-Kazooie spiritual successor series on Xbox consoles.
body: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition was announced on Nov. 25 and is a current-gen upgrade for the 2019 platformer. While the first Yooka-Laylee game emulated the feel of Banjo-Kazooie, Impossible Lair draws inspiration from Rare's work on the Donkey Kong Country series. Its Definitive Edition will launch on Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Windows PC on Dec. 15, and it will vastly improve the lighting, textures, frame rate, and resolution.

While Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair came out on Xbox One in 2019, an Xbox Series X or S version of the Definitive Edition wasn't part of the initial announcement. Players asked Playtonic about this, so the developer took to X to explain why it wasn't coming to the console. "We've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," Playtonic explained, admitting later in the statement that "the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time."

body: A reimagining of Virginia Woolf’s classic novel, “Clarissa” follows a society woman as she prepares to host a party at her home in Lagos, where she’ll unexpectedly encounter once-intimate friends from her youth. Reviewing the film in Cannes, Variety ’s Jessica Kiang heralded the Esiri duo’s “quietly dazzling Nigerian reinterpretation of ‘Mrs. Dalloway,’” praising “a superb Sophie Okonedo, radiant with melancholy, at the heart of its remarkably well-cast ensemble,” which includes David Oyelowo (“Selma”), India Amarteifio (“Queen Charlotte”), Ayo Edebiri (“The Bear”) and Toheeb Jimoh (“Ted Lasso,” “Industry”).

“Expanding in ambition and feeling from their promising debut ‘ This Is My Desire ’ (aka ‘Eyimofe’),” wrote Kiang, “the Esiris cast a perceptive eye over the elite social constellation that has fallen into orbit around this dutiful but unfulfilled society wife, and have nothing but compassion for her as she spins slowly around and around at its center: loved by some, resented by others, admired by all — and totally alone.”

body: In a story arc refreshing the idea of a modern, “cradle to grave” welfare state, the document will, according to some sources, define what the state can do for young people, those in middle age, and older people.

There is furious lobbying going on right now to determine what goes in the document, which is understandable when the measures that are included will form the basis of policy for at least the next few years, even if the plan itself fails to last intact for a decade. Burnham has pledged to publish it by mid-December.

The public is almost certainly going to read comforting words about the need to lift more children out of poverty and support them into well-paid jobs. That is Alan Milburn’s victory after his landmark report earlier this month.
However, people need Burnham to say more about how he intends to approach this subject; will he revert to language that emphasises how individual measures increase economic growth?

highlights.title: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light
highlights.summary: German company Q.ANT is trying to cut the amount of energy required to run AI models by using light to perform the toughest calculations.
body: As artificial intelligence becomes an unavoidable part of everyday life and models become ever more sophisticated, the cost of the energy required to run the technology is ballooning.

To rein in runaway costs, AI labs and cloud providers are trying to build new data centers in places with cheap and plentiful renewable energy— like Scandinavia. But logistical challenges, a scarcity of key components, and a swell of anti-data center protests are getting in the way.

An expanding field of hardware startups, among them German company Q.ANT, is coming at the problem from a different direction: by developing a new breed of chip— photonic processors —meant to minimize the amount of energy that AI models consume.

Whereas regular GPUs transmit and process data by shuffling electrons around, photonic processors use waves of light. Because light doesn’t generate heat as it travels and allows more data to be processed simultaneously, photonic processors supposedly consume less energy and require minimal cooling—one of the largest sources of cost for data centers.

highlights.title: Horse racing live: Newcastle and Newbury’s Coral Gold Cup latest updates
highlights.summary: Willie Mullins’s Road To Home one of star attractions. Join the conversation by emailing Greg Wood. Off to Newcastle next for the Rehearsal Chase at 1.25, a three-mile handicap chase that has – in the fairly distant past, admittedly – been a pointer towards the Gold Cup and Grand National.
body: Wendigo, a seven-year-old gelding who races for 4,000 members of the RC Syndicate, was a hugely popular winner of the Coral Gold Cup Handicap Chase at Newbury on Saturday, one of the most prestigious and historic events in the National Hunt calendar.

Sent off favourite at 11-4, Wendigo was not travelling as well as several of his market rivals through the first two miles of the £250k contest. He stayed on best of all in the long home straight, however, and Gavin Sheehan, Wendigo’s jockey, had a three-length lead over the last. Regent’s Stroll, the top weight, ran on strongly up the run-in but was still one-and-a-quarter lengths adrift at the line.

“It’s another dream come true,” Jamie Snowden, the winner’s trainer, said. “It’s one of the most valuable handicap chases outside of the Grand National and to come and win it with a horse that has become the Newbury people’s horse is a dream.

“The further he went, the better he was going and he probably got there a little too soon and idled in front. He’s tough and brave, just like his jockey, and you’re never certain you’ve won until the line comes, but you always thought he would hold on.”

highlights.title: Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival Opens With Lawrence Fajardo’s ‘Silenced Nights’ and a Call to Face Reality
highlights.summary: The 21st Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF) kicked off Nov. 28 at the Empire XXI cinema in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, with Filipino director Lawrence Fajardo’s thriller “Silenced Nights” as its opening film. The evening’s gentle drizzle stopped shortly after the ceremony began.
body: The ceremony then took a political turn. Festival president Ifa Isfansyah and festival director Budi Irawanto invited the audience to reflect on the unsettling state of the world, pointing to natural and political crises and social inequality that threaten people’s safety.

“A festival must not be a space separate from reality; it cannot just be a place to escape from problems out there. Instead, a festival must be a space to face reality, open up conversations, bring together various perspectives, and preserve the possibility of critical thinking,” said Irawanto, who then asked attendees to stand for a moment of silence.

Fajardo thanked the festival and said the film is personally meaningful to him. “Silenced Nights,” set against extrajudicial killings in a Philippine urban community, played in the Platform competition at the Toronto International Film Festival in September.

Indonesian singer Mondo Gascaro closed the night with a live set that opened with the soothing “Butiran Angin” and took in “Senandung Lagu Lama,” from Usmar Ismail’s 1956 musical “Tiga Dara” (“Three Maidens”); “Apatis,” composed for Nugroho’s “Kucumbu Tubuh Indahku” (“Memories of My Body”); and “Dan Bila.”

highlights.summary: We wouldn’t normally recommend a bad camera, but we’ll make an exception for the Kodak Charmera. As my colleague Andrew Liszewski pointed out in his review, the tiny retro keychain camera takes pretty lackluster photos, yet it’s charming enough that he kept using it anyway.
body: The tiny keychain camera is a ton of fun to use, even if its photos are laughably bad.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The Charmera is small enough to carry on your keys and comes in a blind box, so you won’t know which of the six retro designs or the rarer transparent version you’re getting until you open it. It’s a simple point-and-shoot with a tiny LCD screen, and its 1,440x1,080-pixel photos often look fuzzy and washed out. Some of the built-in effects can make the results more interesting, though. Liszewski had some fun with the black-and-white mode and found that the red, blue, yellow, and gray pixel filters could produce bolder two-tone images. Video and audio quality are poor, too, and you can’t adjust much to improve them. Still, for a $30 keychain, it offers a surprising amount to play with.

The Charmera isn’t something you’d want to rely on for an important occasion, but it can be fun to experiment with. Liszewski found that even though most pictures weren’t worth keeping, he’d occasionally get one interesting enough to share. That makes it a fun stocking stuffer for someone who loves cute, unusual gadgets.

highlights.title: Marvel Snap's Black Friday Deal Went Terribly Wrong
highlights.summary: Marvel Snap players had been saving up for Black Friday deals on Collector's Packs that could net them new cards. When the daily reset that was supposed to kick off the discount finally rolled around, though, something went wrong.
body: Card acquisition is expensive in Marvel Snap. The cheapest way to get new Series 5 cards — the highest series tier most competitive new card releases fall under — is to spend 4,000 Collector's Tokens for a Series 5 Collector's Pack that will randomly snag the player an older Series 5 card they don't own. Collector's Tokens are earned slowly in-game or bought with Gold, Marvel Snap's premium currency.

As a result, players look for discounts or cheaper ways to get new cards. After last week's update, Marvel Snap dataminers discovered a planned discount on standard Collector's Packs for Black Friday. During this deal, players were supposed to be able to buy up to five Series 5 packs for just 3,200 Collector's Tokens per pack (Series 3 and 4 packs would also be discounted). While it was only a 20% discount, this was still going to be a great deal for those who stockpiled tokens and could speed up their journey to becoming collection-complete.

highlights.summary: When elderly parents need looking after, it’s usually their daughters who do the bulk of the work – as highlighted by a viral Saturday Night Live skit. Here, siblings share how to spread the load more evenly. When Simran and her older brother were growing up, he was always the golden boy.
body: “It’s funny how the tables have turned,” she says. “The person they spoiled is the person who has never been there for them, never even bought my mum and dad a birthday card. I had dreams and ambitions of things I wanted to do, but I can’t pursue them now.”

As a woman of south Asian heritage, Simran says she is also battling an extra cultural expectation that she will look after her parents. “I had a friend say: ‘But you are really blessed to have to do seva,’” she says, referring to the Sikh tradition of selfless service for others. “And I say: ‘Blessed in what way?’ Of course I want to be there for my mum … but people don’t get it unless they’re a carer, how lonely and isolating it is, how it affects your mental health.”

highlights.title: GTA 6’s Criminal Profile Isn’t a Morality Spectrum – It’s an RPG Class System
highlights.summary: Doing violent crimes changes your criminal profile in GTA 6, but this isn't a punishment for being "evil" - it's a new take on the RPG class system.
body: This is an opinion piece from writer Samuel Horti. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games.

GTA 6 is a tender love story about a couple clinging to each other through chaos, about the impossible lengths people go for their families, about second chances and forgiveness, about the small moments of romance – watching TV entwined on the sofa, holding hands on the beach, an unexpected compliment – in which relationships bloom.
It is also a game where you can grab a bystander with a digger's claw and squeeze until their head pops.

Modern GTA games have sometimes struggled to square attempts at serious protagonists, or at least protagonists with any depth or humanity, with their inevitable open-world crime sprees. It's hard to take a potentially poignant cut-scene seriously when you've just mowed down 25 pedestrians with a machine gun, and pelted another dozen with RPGs.

highlights.title: Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5
highlights.summary: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
body: Thanks to our partnership with AWS, we were lucky enough to get access to a Trainium3 machine ( trn3.48xlarge, 64 NeuronCores) for a month. We spent most of the month testing Hugging Face models on it, and getting more of them to work.
With five days left, I allowed myself a little fun. When you have a Ferrari, every now and then you want to take it out on the track. So I asked myself: what if I tried to generate videos?

I picked LTX-2.5 from Lightricks, which generates video and sound together. By the end, once the models were loaded, a 10-second clip with sound took 22 to 23 s to generate, on half of the machine. Here is the result.

I had two goals. The first was to see how easy it is to generate videos with diffusers on Trainium3. Not the simple clips from the examples: I wanted to make short films from a script, closer to a real use case, like drafting a movie. The second was performance. I wanted to get close to what you get with CUDA, or with LTX's own API.

highlights.title: 007 First Light's Brilliant Tutorial Is a Game Direction Miracle
highlights.summary: The 007 First Light tutorial is the platonic ideal of a perfect video game tutorial. IO Interactive reveals how it came together.
body: How did James Bond become James Bond? Through a 1980s movie montage, of course! Come on. Everyone knows that one.

007 First Light, IO Interactive’s 2026 take on James Bond and the greatest 007 game of the century (so far), did a whole lot of shaking up. It’s billed as an origin story for Ian Fleming’s famous spy, coloring in the background of a character often wrapped in intrigue. It’s also IO Interactive’s first foray outside of the Hitman-iverse in 16 years, allowing the studio ample room to flex its action chops. But as we approach the end of the year — with all of the reflection and end-of-year debates that incurs — 007 First Light perhaps stands out most for one innovation: its killer tutorial.

“It was maybe also one of the hardest tutorials in gaming history, I could imagine. I don't know. I'm not gonna speak for others, but it was so hard,” Hakan Abrak, game director on 007 First Ligh t, told Polygon in an interview. “And you know, we were nervous whether it's gonna work out, because who wants to be in a tutorial for such a long time, right?”
